question: On five distinct precommitted subgroup targets, do the frozen IC candidate and Sage's 20-partition rho both recover each same-point scalar in alternating order, and what online intervals are observed on one local host?
shared_setup: reconstruct the immutable candidate base and pair index, load and replay the previously solved 125 base logs before any target clock; record setup duration once
ic: call the frozen candidate's ic_online function with only the public target point; use its five exclusive target-online phases and scalar replay
rho: call installed Sage 20-partition discrete_log_rho on the same public point with a deterministic coordinate hash, a new seed 93000+fixture_index, no cross-target table; charge scalar replay
calibration: 512 deterministic subgroup additions before and after each pair, outside target clocks; record both intervals and flag ratios above 1.25 without replacing any pair
resource_envelope: one local macOS checked Sage process, one CPU worker per arm, 8 GiB observed RSS stop threshold; no dedicated allocation
claim_boundary: exploratory local five-distinct-target correctness and timing panel; no Tier 0/1 isolation or speedup promotion
